I will keep to the wheat-maize rotation that fits Quzhou County best. On my land, that is still the most reliable way to use the full year, match local temperature and rainfall patterns, and keep cash flow steady. At the start of the season, my winter wheat is already the core crop, so I will manage it carefully through spring with moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations, and targeted pest control rather than spraying excessively. After wheat harvest, I will go straight into summer maize with a high-yield hybrid, because maize follows well after wheat here and makes good use of the summer heat and rain. Because I am well educated, I would rather manage inputs precisely than chase yield with heavy fertilizer or too many pesticide applications. I will use improved or hybrid seed, keep nitrogen as the main nutrient, add balanced phosphorus and potassium, and choose rotary tillage for speed and practicality between crops. My goal is stable yield, manageable labor, and lower production risk across the whole year.
